# Home Safety Solutions

> Clinician-led home safety assessment and hospital discharge readiness in the Tampa Bay area of Florida. Every assessment is done personally by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP, who looks at the person, their equipment and the home together. In person around Tampa Bay; by video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio. Private pay. Tagline: Safer Homes. Brighter Tomorrows.

Home Safety Solutions is a registered fictitious name and product line of Practical Innovations, Inc.

## Clinician

- Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP: Doctor of Physical Therapy and RESNA Assistive Technology Professional (ATP).
- More than 35 years of physical therapy practice, including service as a VA Home Safety Coordinator on a home-based primary care team.
- Trained in aging-in-place design and modification through the National Association of Home Builders. Teaches in Doctor of Physical Therapy programs.
- Licensed physical therapist in Florida (PT39370), New York (011600) and Ohio (PT020959).

## Services and prices (USD)

- Initial Consultation: $50. A 30-minute phone call. Every service starts here. The $50 is credited toward any visit booked within 30 days.
- Home Safety Visit: $250 in the home, $175 by video. Fall-risk and home safety assessment, 60 to 120 minutes, photo report within 48 hours, fall risk screening using the CDC STEADI approach, debrief call.
- Ready for Discharge: $250 in the home, $175 by video. Checks whether the home can support a patient leaving the hospital or rehab. Ends with one readiness rating: Green, Yellow or Red.
- Right Home Assessment: $250, in person only. Checks whether a house fits the person who will live there, before buying, renting or moving.
- Deep dives, added to a core assessment: Storm Ready Audit $75 (in person only), Assistive Technology Consultation $75, Remote Caregiving Plan $150 (does not include a Contractor Consultation).
- Contractor Consultation: $150. A contractor-ready prescription and one call with the client's contractor.
- Build Verify Visit: $150. Checks that finished work matches the specifications.
- Rush scheduling within 48 hours: add $50.
- Membership: $600 per year, or $55 per month with a 12-month commitment. Only for people who have had a core assessment, and only for homes inside the in-person service area.

## Payment

Private pay only. Home Safety Solutions does not bill or accept Medicare, Medicaid, the VA or any insurance.

## Service area

- In person: about a 60-minute drive from Apollo Beach, Florida, including Sun City Center and the surrounding Tampa Bay area. Address checker: https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area
- By video: homes anywhere in Florida, New York or Ohio, where Dr. L'HommeDieu is licensed. The patient must be in one of those states during the session. Family can join from anywhere.

## Independence policy

Independent. No referral fees, no commissions and no payments from contractors, installers, suppliers, equipment companies or device makers. Home Safety Solutions assesses and recommends; it does not sell equipment or do construction or installation. It follows a "Nothing About Me...Without Me" policy: nothing is changed, recommended or set in motion without the person's say.

# Is the home ready for the person coming home?

Hospitals and rehab centers get people ready to leave. No one is assigned to check whether the house is ready to receive them. We do.

A Doctor of Physical Therapy and RESNA-certified Assistive Technology Professional assesses the person, their equipment, and the home together, then gives you a clear written plan you can act on this week.

[Book a $50 consultation](https://intakeq.com/booking/zm1cyz?serviceId=7c400002-9dcd-4689-a8e5-1e075c4c5d9c)
30-minute phone call. $50, credited toward any visit within 30 days.

- DPTDoctor of Physical Therapy

- ATPRESNA Assistive Technology Professional

- 35+ yearsPT experience & Former VA Home Safety Coordinator

In person within the Tampa Bay area. By video for patients and homes in Florida, New York, or Ohio.

- 1 Entry step with no rail

- 2 Sunken living room edge

- 3 Sliding door track to the lanai

- 4 Dark path from bed to bath

- 5 Low toilet, high tub wall

## Why the home often gets missed

Every discharge plan assumes a home that can support it. Most of the time, nobody has looked.

### Discharge plans are written for the patient, not the house

Case managers work under time pressure without training in home environments. Home health therapy starts after the person is already home. Contractors can build, but they do not assess how a person moves.

### Falls are where the gap shows up first

About one in four adults age 65 and older falls each year, and falls lead to roughly one million hospital stays a year. Many start with a step, a threshold, or a trip to the bathroom in the dark.

### Florida homes bring their own hazards

Sunken living rooms, pool decks, slider tracks, and garage entry steps. Then hurricane season, when a power outage becomes a medical event for anyone on oxygen or a powered bed.

Fall figures: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, [Facts About Falls](https://www.cdc.gov/falls/data-research/facts-stats/index.html), 2026.

What we do about it. We assess the person, the home, and the people who help, in person or by video. You get a photo report, a prioritized hazard list, and specific recommendations. When changes need a builder, you choose one and hire them directly. We never take money from contractors.

## How it works

-
### Talk with us
A 30 minute phone consultation to work through your needs, gather the important details, and match you to the right service. $50, credited toward any visit you book within 30 days.

-
### We assess the person and the home
In person, or by guided video before a hospital discharge. We look at how the person moves, not just at the house.

-
### You get a written plan
A photo report, a prioritized hazard list, and recommendations, delivered to a secure portal, followed by a call to walk through it.

-
### Changes get made right
We write exact specifications for the contractor you choose, then verify the finished work before anyone relies on it.

## One clear answer before discharge day

Every Ready for Discharge report ends with a single readiness rating across ten areas of daily life, so everyone knows what has to happen first.

### Green
The home is ready for this person as it is today.

### !Yellow
Ready once the listed items are done before arrival.

### xRed
A gap that cannot be closed by arrival day. We call the family the same day.

The rating describes the home's readiness for this person. It is not medical clearance.

[See how Ready for Discharge works](https://www.homesafety.solutions/ready-for-discharge)

## We never take money from builders or equipment sellers

Many home safety checks are done by the company that wants to sell you the renovation. We separate the two. We assess and prescribe. You choose from vetted, licensed contractors, and you contract with them directly.

No referral fees. No commissions. No payments from contractors, installers, suppliers, equipment companies, or device makers.

[How we vet contractors](https://www.homesafety.solutions/contractors)

### What you receive after a Home Safety Visit

- A photo report of every room we assessed

- A prioritized hazard list: fix now, within 30 days, and planned

- Fall risk screening using the CDC STEADI approach

- Specific recommendations for equipment, routines, and changes

- A debrief call to answer every question

## Nothing about you, without you

Your home and your choices stay yours. We hold a strict "Nothing About Me...Without Me" policy: nothing gets changed, recommended, or set in motion without your say.

We assess, explain the options, and wait for your decision. You are always the one who decides what happens next.

### What this means for you

- No change is made to your home without your consent

- Every recommendation is explained before you decide

- You choose which items to act on, and when

- You can pause, decline, or change your mind at any point

- Your priorities lead the plan, start to finish

Dr. L'HommeDieu has practiced physical therapy for more than 35 years, including long service as a VA Home Safety Coordinator on a home-based primary care team. He holds the Assistive Technology Professional credential from Rehabilitation Engineering and Assistive Technology Society of North America (RESNA) and is trained in aging-in-place design and modification through the National Association of Home Builders. He teaches in Doctor of Physical Therapy programs.

Every assessment is done by Dr. L'HommeDieu personally.

Home Safety Visit

# A safer home, on your terms

You know your home better than anyone. We help you see it the way a physical therapist would, so you can keep living there with confidence.

$250 in your home$175 by video

[Start with a $50 consultation](https://intakeq.com/booking/zm1cyz?serviceId=7c400002-9dcd-4689-a8e5-1e075c4c5d9c)
30-minute phone call. $50, credited toward any visit within 30 days.

In short

A Home Safety Visit is a fall-risk and home safety assessment done personally by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, a Doctor of Physical Therapy and RESNA Assistive Technology Professional. It is for adults who have had a fall or near fall, or who find stairs, the tub or getting up from a chair harder than before. It costs $250 in your home around Tampa Bay, or $175 by video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio.

Reviewed by [Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about). Last updated September 29, 2026.

## Key facts

Price
$250 in your home, or $175 by video

Format
In person around Tampa Bay (see our [service area](https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area)). By video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio.

Length
60 to 120 minutes

Done by
[Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about)

You receive
A photo report within 48 hours, a prioritized hazard list, a fall risk screening using the CDC STEADI approach, and a debrief call

How to start
A $50 Initial Consultation, a 30-minute phone call.

## Is this for you?

- You have had a fall or a near fall.

- You have started holding on to furniture to get around.

- Stairs, the tub or getting up from a chair takes more effort than it used to.

- You are coming home from a hospital stay. For that, see [Ready for Discharge](https://www.homesafety.solutions/ready-for-discharge).

## What happens

The visit takes 60 to 120 minutes. Dr. L'HommeDieu watches how you get in and out of the house, the bed, the chair, the shower and the car. He asks about your day, from the first trip to the bathroom in the morning to the last lock of the door at night.

We look at three things together: you, your home and the people who help you. That is what makes this different from a checklist.

## What you get

- A photo report of your home, with the concerns marked

- A prioritized list: what to fix now, within 30 days, and what to plan for

- A fall risk screening using the CDC STEADI approach. STEADI stands for Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths and Injuries, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's standard way for clinicians to screen for fall risk.

- Plain recommendations for equipment, lighting and daily routines

- A debrief call to answer your questions

Your report arrives within 48 hours of the visit. You decide what to change. If you want work done, we can write exact instructions for the contractor you choose.

## Nothing about you, without you

Your home and your choices stay yours. We hold a strict "Nothing About Me...Without Me" policy: nothing gets changed, recommended or set in motion without your say. We assess, explain the options and wait for your decision.

## Add a deep dive

Your report already touches on each of these. A deep dive goes further, with its own written plan. Dr. L'HommeDieu can add one on the consultation call.

- [Remote Caregiving Plan](https://www.homesafety.solutions/remote-caregiving)+$150

- [Storm Ready Audit](https://www.homesafety.solutions/storm-ready) in person only+$75

## Common questions

**Should family be there?**
Yes, if possible. The person who lives in the home should be present, and anyone who helps with care is welcome, in person or by phone or video.

**Do you install anything?**
No. We assess and recommend. You choose who does the work. This keeps our advice independent.

**Can you send the report to my doctor?**
Yes, with your written permission. You sign the release in our secure client portal naming your doctor, and we send the report directly. Sharing it helps your care team understand your home and your daily routines.

[More questions and answers](https://www.homesafety.solutions/faq)

Ready for Discharge

# Is the home ready for them to come home?

Check the home before the patient leaves the hospital or rehab. One guided visit, a written report within 24 hours, and one clear rating.

$250 in your home$175 by video

[Start with a $50 consultation](https://intakeq.com/booking/zm1cyz?serviceId=7c400002-9dcd-4689-a8e5-1e075c4c5d9c)
30-minute phone call. $50, credited toward any visit within 30 days.

In short

Ready for Discharge is a check of the home before a patient leaves the hospital or rehab, done personally by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP. It is for families and discharge planners who need to know whether the home can support the person on day one. It costs $250 in the home around Tampa Bay, or $175 by video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio, and ends with one rating: Green, Yellow or Red.

Discharge readiness means whether the home, the equipment and the people helping are ready to support the patient safely from the first day home.

Reviewed by [Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about). Last updated September 29, 2026.

## Key facts

Price
$250 in the home, or $175 by video

Format
In person around Tampa Bay (see our [service area](https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area)). By video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio.

Length
About an hour

Done by
[Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about)

You receive
A Green, Yellow or Red readiness rating across ten areas, a written report within 24 hours, a call to go over every Red and Yellow item, and a check-in call seven days after discharge

How to start
A $50 Initial Consultation, a 30-minute phone call.

## Is this for you?

- A family member is in the hospital or rehab and will be discharged soon.

- You are not sure the home can support them on day one.

- You live out of the area and need to know what to set up before they arrive.

- You are a discharge planner who wants the home checked before the patient leaves.

## What happens

-
### The $50 consultation
A family member or discharge planner books the call and gives the expected discharge date. Dr. L'HommeDieu schedules the discharge visit with you on that call.

-
### Get the home ready
For a video visit, the family receives our [Home Video Walkthrough Guide](https://www.homesafety.solutions/walkthrough-guide): a tape measure, good light and a charged phone are most of it. Forms are handled in our secure client portal.

-
### The visit
About an hour. Dr. L'HommeDieu talks with the patient about their daily routine and concerns, then walks the home with the family: entry, the path to the bedroom, bathroom, kitchen and where equipment will go.

-
### Report within 24 hours
The Discharge Home Readiness Report is posted to the portal, followed by a call to go over every Red and Yellow item.

-
### Seven-day check-in
A short call after the patient is home: were the must-do items done, any falls or ER visits, anything new.

## What you get

- A readiness rating across ten areas: getting in, moving through, bed and transfers, bathroom, kitchen and meals, equipment, people and caregiver coverage, supplies and routines, safety and emergencies, and follow-up

- A written report within 24 hours

- A call to go over every Red and Yellow item

- A check-in call seven days after discharge

### Green: ready
The home can support this person as it is.

### !Yellow: ready once listed items are done
Specific changes must be completed before arrival.

### xRed: a gap that cannot close by arrival day
We call the family the same day, and the discharge planner with authorization.

The rating describes the home's readiness for this person. It is not medical clearance. Sessions are not recorded.

# Will this home work, now and in ten years?

Before you buy, rent or move, find out whether the house fits the person who will live there, and what it would take to make it work.

The Right Home Assessment checks whether a house fits the person who will live there, now and in ten years, before you buy, rent or move. Storm Ready Audit

# Ready before the power goes out

In Florida, a multi-day power outage is a medical event for anyone who depends on oxygen, a powered bed or refrigerated medicine. Plan before June 1.

+$75 deep dive, added to any core assessmentRequires one core assessment

[Start with a $50 consultation](https://intakeq.com/booking/zm1cyz?serviceId=7c400002-9dcd-4689-a8e5-1e075c4c5d9c)
30-minute phone call. $50, credited toward your core assessment within 30 days.

In short

The Storm Ready Audit is a hurricane and power outage plan for a home where someone depends on oxygen, a powered bed or refrigerated medicine. It is a $75 deep dive added to a core assessment, done in person by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP, inside our Tampa Bay service area. Hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30.

Reviewed by [Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about). Last updated September 29, 2026.

## Key facts

Price
+$75, added to a core assessment. Included with Membership.

Format
In person only, added to an in-home core assessment inside our [Tampa Bay service area](https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area)

Done by
[Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about)

You receive
An inventory of every power-dependent device and its backup, a medicine and cooling plan, an evacuation plan, and a written household plan

How to start
A $50 Initial Consultation, a 30-minute phone call.

## How this fits with your core assessment

Every core assessment report touches on this topic. The deep dive goes further, with its own written plan. Dr. L'HommeDieu can add it to your visit on the consultation call.

In your core reportA flag on powered equipment and heat risks.

In the deep diveEvery powered device listed with its backup, plus cooling, medicine, evacuation and family contact plans for outages.

## Is this for you?

- Someone in the home depends on oxygen, a powered bed or other medical equipment.

- Medicine in the home needs refrigeration.

- Evacuating would be hard because of mobility or transport.

- The family has no written plan for a hurricane, heat or a long outage.

Hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30. The best time to plan is April and May.

## What happens

Dr. L'HommeDieu comes to the home and goes through every piece of equipment, every medicine that needs cold storage, and the plan for heat, evacuation and getting help. The whole family can join.

## What you get

- An inventory of every power-dependent device and how long each can run on battery

- Backup power options, and which ones need a licensed electrician

- Medicine storage when the refrigerator is off

- Heat: keeping cool safely without air conditioning

- Evacuation logistics, including mobility, transport and who goes where

- A written household plan the whole family can follow

## Free Storm Ready checklist

Use this to get started on your own. Print it and keep it by the phone.

### Before the season

- List every device that needs power and its battery run time.

- Ask your equipment supplier about backup batteries and an outage plan.

- Ask your pharmacist how to store each medicine if power fails.

- Find your evacuation zone on your county's emergency management website.

- If you depend on electricity for medical equipment, ask your county about its special needs registry.

- Tell your electric utility if you use life-sustaining equipment.

- Keep a written list of medicines, doctors and equipment settings in a waterproof bag.

### When a storm is coming

- Charge every device, spare battery and phone.

- Fill prescriptions early and gather a two-week supply if you can.

- Decide now: stay, go to family, or go to a shelter. Arrange transport.

- Clear walkways and put lights, shoes and a walker by the bed.

- Never run a generator indoors, in a garage or near windows.

Print this checklist

Assistive Technology Consultation

# The right equipment, fitted to the person and the home

Walkers, shower chairs, lift chairs, medical alert pendants and smart home devices are often bought from an ad and end up unused in a closet. We match the technology to the person, check that it fits the home, and put the recommendations in writing so you can buy anywhere.

+$75 deep dive, added to any core assessmentRequires one core assessment

[Start with a $50 consultation](https://intakeq.com/booking/zm1cyz?serviceId=7c400002-9dcd-4689-a8e5-1e075c4c5d9c)
30-minute phone call. $50, credited toward your core assessment within 30 days.

In short

The Assistive Technology Consultation is an independent review of the equipment a person uses or needs, such as walkers, shower chairs, lift chairs, fall alerts and smart home devices. It is done by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, a RESNA Assistive Technology Professional, who takes no payments from equipment companies or device makers. It is a $75 deep dive added to a core assessment, in person around Tampa Bay or by video in Florida, New York and Ohio.

Reviewed by [Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about). Last updated September 29, 2026.

## Key facts

Price
+$75, added to a core assessment. Included with Membership.

Format
In person around Tampa Bay (see our [service area](https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area)). By video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio.

Done by
[Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about)

You receive
Written recommendations with specifications, training notes and a follow-up call

How to start
A $50 Initial Consultation, a 30-minute phone call.

## How this fits with your core assessment

Every core assessment report touches on this topic. The deep dive goes further, with its own written plan. Dr. L'HommeDieu can add it to your visit on the consultation call.

In your core reportThe equipment the home needs most.

In the deep diveAn independent review of the assistive equipment the person uses or needs, with a specific focus on technology.

## Is this for you?

- You have equipment at home that is not being used, or does not fit.

- You are about to buy a walker, shower chair, lift chair or fall alert and want to get it right.

- Someone's mobility has changed and their equipment may no longer suit them.

- You want fall detection or smart home help but do not know where to start.

Need a full system for family to support someone from a distance? See the [Remote Caregiving Plan](https://www.homesafety.solutions/remote-caregiving).

## What happens

We review the person, their routines and the home, then everything they use or might need:

- Equipment already in the home: walkers, canes, wheelchairs, shower chairs, commodes, transfer aids and lift chairs. Is it fitted correctly, used safely, and still right for how the person moves today?

- Fall detection and emergency response: wearable and passive options, matched to the person's routines and willingness to use them

- Smart home safety: lighting, motion and door sensors, voice control and video check-ins for family

- Power dependence: which devices need backup power during storms and outages

- Home fit: whether doorways, turning space, flooring and bathrooms can support the equipment

## What you get

- A written recommendation list with specifications, so you can shop anywhere

- Notes on training for the user and caregivers

- A follow-up call to confirm the equipment works in daily life

## Why an ATP?

An Assistive Technology Professional (ATP) is certified by RESNA, the Rehabilitation Engineering and Assistive Technology Society of North America, after meeting education and experience requirements and passing a national exam. The credential shows skill in assessing a person's needs and environment, matching them with the right technology, training users and following up. Medicare requires an ATP to be involved in certain complex power wheelchair decisions.

## What we do not do

We advise; we do not sell. We do not supply equipment or bill insurance for it, and we accept no fees or commissions from equipment companies or suppliers. When equipment requires a prescription, such as a power wheelchair, we provide the assessment and recommendations for your physician and supplier.

Remote Caregiving Plan

# Caring for someone from far away

When you can't be there every day, the right technology can help you know they are safe. Most families buy devices one at a time and end up with apps that don't work together and alerts no one trusts. We design the whole system first, a qualified installer puts it in, and we train your family to use it.

+$150 deep dive, added to any core assessmentRequires one core assessment

[Start with a $50 consultation](https://intakeq.com/booking/zm1cyz?serviceId=7c400002-9dcd-4689-a8e5-1e075c4c5d9c)
30-minute phone call. $50, credited toward your core assessment within 30 days.

In short

The Remote Caregiving Plan is a room-by-room technology plan that helps family support someone from a distance, covering fall detection, safe entry, video check-ins, lighting and stove safety. It is designed by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP, and is a $150 deep dive added to a core assessment, in person around Tampa Bay or by video in Florida, New York and Ohio. It does not include a Contractor Consultation or 24-hour monitoring.

Reviewed by [Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about). Last updated September 29, 2026.

## Key facts

Price
+$150, added to a core assessment. Included with Membership.

Format
In person around Tampa Bay (see our [service area](https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area)). By video for homes in Florida, New York and Ohio.

Done by
[Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about)

You receive
A room-by-room plan with devices, specifications, placement and priorities, one family training session by video (up to 60 minutes), and a follow-up call after installation

Not included
A Contractor Consultation ($150, available separately), installation, or 24-hour monitoring

How to start
A $50 Initial Consultation, a 30-minute phone call.

## How this fits with your core assessment

Every core assessment report touches on this topic. The deep dive goes further, with its own written plan. Dr. L'HommeDieu can add it to your visit on the consultation call.

In your core reportWhere a fall could go unseen, and how help would get in.

In the deep diveA room-by-room technology plan: fall detection, safe entry, video check-ins, lighting and stove safety, with family training by video.

## Is this for you?

- You live out of the area or out of state from someone you care for.

- An older adult lives alone and wants to stay in their own home.

- The family is adjusting after a hospital stay, a fall or a new diagnosis.

- You have bought devices that are not working together.

## What happens

-
### The $50 consultation
We talk through goals, concerns and who is involved in care, and schedule a core assessment with the Remote Caregiving deep dive added.

-
### Assessment
During your core assessment, in the home or by video, we look at the person, their daily routines, the home layout, Wi-Fi and cell signal, devices already in place, and each family member's role.

-
### Your written plan
A room-by-room plan with devices, specifications, placement and priorities.

-
### Installation
You choose a qualified installer and pay them directly. You share your written plan with them. The plan does not include a Contractor Consultation. If you want us to prepare a contractor-ready prescription and talk with your installer, add a [Contractor Consultation](https://www.homesafety.solutions/services#contractor-consultation) for $150.

-
### Family training
A video session to set up alerts and practice what each person does when an alert comes in, then a follow-up call after installation.

### What the plan covers

- Fall detection: wearable and camera-free options, matched to how the person lives

- Safe entry: smart door locks with separate, scheduled codes for aides, family and emergency responders

- The front door: video doorbells so the person and family can see who is there

- Staying in touch: a video calling setup simple enough to use every day

- Lighting: automatic lighting from bed to bathroom and at entrances

- Environmental controls: voice or app control matched to hand function, hearing, vision and memory

- Kitchen safety: automatic stove shutoff options for electric and gas ranges

- Heat and cooling: thermostat alerts when the home gets too hot or too cold

- Storms and outages: what still works without power or internet, and a simple low-tech plan

## What you get

- A written Remote Caregiving Plan: room-by-room devices, specifications, placement and priorities

- An Alert and Response Plan: who receives each alert and what they do

- A Storm and Outage Plan

- A Home Monitoring Agreement, reviewed with the person being monitored or their legal representative

- One family training session by video (up to 60 minutes, any number of family members) and a follow-up call after installation

## Qualified installers

Many plug-in devices can be set up by family, with our guidance by video. Hardwired lighting, door locks, stove shutoffs, thermostats and backup power go to qualified installers, such as licensed electricians, security and low-voltage installers, and HVAC contractors. Any work on a gas range goes to a licensed gas contractor. You choose your installer, contract with them and pay them directly. A Contractor Consultation is not part of the plan; it can be added for $150. [See our Contractor Network](https://www.homesafety.solutions/contractors).

## Privacy and respect

Monitoring should protect independence, not take it away. We plan with the person being monitored, not just about them. We do not recommend cameras in bedrooms or bathrooms. Health information in your plan is protected under HIPAA.

## What we do not do

We do not sell devices, and we accept no fees or commissions from device makers, retailers, monitoring companies or installers. We do not provide 24-hour monitoring or emergency response. In an emergency, call 911.

Membership

# Peace of mind, all year

## Is this for you?

- You have had one of our core assessments and want the home re-checked as needs change.

- Someone in the home depends on power for medical equipment and needs a plan every season.

- Family lives at a distance and wants regular check-ins.

- You want to be first in line when something changes.

# Compare your options
Plain side-by-side answers to the two questions families ask most before they book.

## Clinician-led assessment vs a contractor's free check

In short

A contractor's free check looks at the house, and it is usually done by the company that would be paid to do the work. A clinician-led assessment from Home Safety Solutions looks at the person, their equipment and the home together, is done by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP, and has no tie to who does the work. It costs $250 in the home or $175 by video.

Clinician-led assessment compared with a contractor's free check

| Question | Clinician-led assessment | Contractor's free check |
| Who looks | A Doctor of Physical Therapy and Assistive Technology Professional | A salesperson or installer |
| What is looked at | The person, their daily routines, their equipment and the home | The house and the products the company sells |
| Fall risk | Screened using the CDC STEADI approach | Not part of a sales visit |
| Paid by contractors? | No. No referral fees, commissions or payments from anyone who does the work | The check is paid for by the sale |
| What you receive | A written report with a prioritized list, and contractor-ready specifications if you need them | A quote |
| Cost | $250 in the home, $175 by video | Free |

A good contractor is still part of the plan. We tell you what the person needs and how it should be built; you choose who builds it. Afterward, a [Build Verify Visit](https://www.homesafety.solutions/faq#home-safety-visits) ($150) checks that the finished work matches the specifications. [How we work with contractors](https://www.homesafety.solutions/contractors).

## Ready for Discharge vs Home Safety Visit

In short

Choose Ready for Discharge when someone is coming home from a hospital or rehab stay and you need to know whether the home can support them on day one. Choose the Home Safety Visit when the person is already home and you want to lower their fall risk. Both are $250 in the home or $175 by video.

Ready for Discharge compared with Home Safety Visit

| Question | Ready for Discharge | Home Safety Visit |
| Best for | A hospital or rehab discharge that is coming up | Someone already living at home |
| Main question | Can the home support this person from the first day? | What could lead to a fall, and what should change first? |
| Result | A Green, Yellow or Red readiness rating across ten areas | A prioritized list of changes and a fall risk screening |
| Report | Within 24 hours | Within 48 hours |
| Follow-up | A call on every Red and Yellow item and a check-in seven days after discharge | A debrief call |
| Cost | $250 in the home, $175 by video | $250 in the home, $175 by video |

Not sure which fits? Every service starts with a $50 Initial Consultation, and Dr. L'HommeDieu will help you choose. See [Ready for Discharge](https://www.homesafety.solutions/ready-for-discharge) and the [Home Safety Visit](https://www.homesafety.solutions/home-safety-visit).

Reviewed by [Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP](https://www.homesafety.solutions/about). Last updated September 29, 2026.

# A clinician, not a salesperson, in your home
Home Safety Solutions exists to close one gap: the space between a discharge plan and the home that has to carry it out.

## Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP

Dr. L'HommeDieu has practiced physical therapy for more than 35 years, including long service as a VA Home Safety Coordinator on a home-based primary care team. He holds the Assistive Technology Professional (ATP) credential from Rehabilitation Engineering and Assistive Technology Society of North America (RESNA). An ATP has met education and experience requirements and passed a national exam on matching people with the right equipment and technology. He is also trained in aging-in-place design and modification through the National Association of Home Builders. Aging in place means living safely and independently in your own home as you get older. Home modification means changes to the house itself, such as grab bars, ramps or wider doorways. He teaches in Doctor of Physical Therapy programs.

He earned his Doctor of Physical Therapy at Touro College and is a doctoral candidate in health education and leadership.

- Doctor of Physical Therapy

- RESNA Assistive Technology Professional

- 35+ years PT experience

- Former VA Home Safety Coordinator

Licensed physical therapist in Florida (PT39370), Ohio (PT020959), and New York (011600). Home Safety Solutions offers in-person visits in the Tampa Bay area and virtual visits in Florida, New York, and Ohio.

### The person first
We assess how someone actually moves, thinks, and gets through the day, then judge the home against that. A hazard list without the person is only half the answer.

### Independent by design
We prescribe; licensed contractors build; you hire them directly. We accept no referral fees, so our recommendations answer only to you.

### Measured results
We follow up at 7 days and track what gets done, falls, and ER visits, so we can prove what works and improve what does not.

## Our framework

Every assessment follows the Systems of Systems approach Dr. L'HommeDieu developed and teaches. It brings together three established lenses: the immediate physical and social environment of the home, the social determinants of health, and the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health. In plain terms: the room, the life around it, and the person in it.

## Practical Innovations

Home Safety Solutions is a product line of Practical Innovations, Inc., Dr. L'HommeDieu's healthcare consulting and education company.

# Frequently asked questions
Can't find your answer? Call us at (813) 867-3372, email info@homesafety.solutions, or book a $50 Initial Consultation.

## Getting Started

**What does Home Safety Solutions do?**
We help older adults and people with disabilities live safely at home. A Doctor of Physical Therapy looks at the person, their daily routines, and their home, then gives you a clear, prioritized plan: what to change, what equipment or technology to use, and who can do the work.

**What is a home safety assessment?**
A home safety assessment is a visit where a trained clinician looks at the person, their equipment and their home together, finds what could lead to a fall or injury, and recommends practical changes. At Home Safety Solutions it is done personally by Dr. Russ L'HommeDieu, DPT, ATP, and you receive a written report with a prioritized list. See the [Home Safety Visit](https://www.homesafety.solutions/home-safety-visit).

**Who is this for?**
Older adults who want to stay in their own home, people coming home from a hospital or rehab stay, families caring for someone nearby or from a distance, and anyone planning a move or a remodel with safety in mind.

**How is this different from a regular home safety checklist?**
A checklist looks at the house. We look at the person in the house: their strength, balance, vision, memory, and daily routines. Our recommendations fit how that person actually moves and lives.

**How do I get started?**
Book a $50 Initial Consultation. It's a 30-minute call with Dr. L'HommeDieu. Its purpose is to work through the full picture of your needs, gather the important details about the person and the home, and match you to the right service. If you need a visit, we schedule it with you on the call. The $50 is credited toward any visit you book within 30 days.

**Is the $50 call worth it if I do not book a visit?**
Yes. Dr. L'HommeDieu listens, answers your questions and gives practical advice as time allows, and tells you honestly whether a visit makes sense. A core assessment adds what a phone call cannot: seeing the person in the actual home, a full assessment and a written plan.

**Which service should I choose?**
You do not have to decide alone. Every service starts with the $50 Initial Consultation, where Dr. L'HommeDieu learns about the person and the home and recommends the right fit. Coming home from a hospital soon? Book the earliest consultation time and he will schedule the discharge visit on that call.

**Do I need a doctor's referral?**
No. Our services are home safety and technology consulting, so you can start with a $50 Initial Consultation without one. With your written permission, we can send a copy of your report to your doctor, and we encourage it. If we notice something that needs medical attention, we will let you know and recommend that you contact your doctor.

**Is this physical therapy treatment?**
No. Our services are home safety and technology consulting. We do not provide hands-on physical therapy treatment. If treatment would help, we will tell you and recommend that you talk with your doctor.

**How is this different from home health physical therapy?**
Home health physical therapy is hands-on treatment that starts after the person is already home. We do not provide treatment. We assess the person, the equipment and the home, often before a discharge or before a fall, and give you a written plan. The two can work together: with your written permission, we can send our report to your care team. See [our comparisons](https://www.homesafety.solutions/compare).

Every service starts with a $50 Initial Consultation, credited toward your core assessment. Core assessments are $250 in your home or $175 by video. Deep dives are $75 each, except the Remote Caregiving Plan at $150.

Your $50 is credited in full toward any visit you book within 30 days of the call. If you go on to have a visit, the call costs you nothing extra.

A closer look at one topic your core report already touches: remote caregiving technology, storm readiness, or assistive equipment. Storm Ready and Assistive Technology are $75 each and the Remote Caregiving Plan is $150, added to a core assessment on the same visit. Storm Ready is in person only.

**Can you give me an example?**
A Ready for Discharge visit in your home is $250. Add a Remote Caregiving deep dive and the total is $400. Your $50 consultation credit brings it to $350.

Yes. For scheduling within 48 hours, add $50 to any visit.

No. Your written report is included in every visit.

No. There are no travel fees. In-home visits are offered only inside our in-person service area, about a 60-minute drive from Apollo Beach. Everywhere else in Florida, New York, or Ohio, visits are by telehealth.

There is no drive and no home visit, so we pass that savings to you.

The card is charged sooner only if the cancellation or no-show policy applies. Any visit you go on to have is charged to the same card, with your $50 credited toward it.

Cancel or reschedule free with at least 24 hours' notice. With less than 24 hours' notice, there is a $50 fee. If no one is home for an in-home visit, the fee is $100; a missed virtual visit is $50. There is never a fee for a hospital stay, a medical emergency, a death in the family, a hurricane watch or warning, or an evacuation order.

A completed visit or delivered report is non-refundable. If we made an error in your report, we will correct it at no charge.

## Reimbursement and Insurance

**Is this covered by insurance?**
Usually not. Medicare and most health plans pay to treat medical conditions, not to make a home safer. Medicare does not cover home modifications or items like grab bars, and it does not cover home technology like smart locks or thermostats. Home Safety Solutions is a private-pay consulting service and does not bill Medicare or insurance. Veterans: the VA may pay for items Medicare does not cover. See the Veterans section below.

**Why doesn't Medicare cover home safety?**
Medicare covers equipment that serves a mainly medical purpose, like wheelchairs, oxygen, and hospital beds. It considers items like grab bars, bath seats, and raised toilet seats to be for comfort or convenience, even though they help prevent falls. Home modifications and home technology fall outside Medicare coverage for the same reason.

**Can I submit it to my insurance myself?**
Yes, you can try. We provide an itemized receipt on request. We cannot guarantee reimbursement.

**Does Medicare Advantage cover any of this?**
Some Medicare Advantage plans offer extra benefits for home safety items, bathroom safety devices, or in-home support. Call the number on your member card and ask about "home safety" or "bathroom safety" benefits.

**Will long-term care insurance pay?**
Some long-term care policies reimburse home modifications or care coordination. Check your policy or call your insurer, and submit your itemized receipt.

**Does Florida Medicaid cover home modifications?**
Members of Florida Medicaid's long-term care program may be able to get home accessibility adaptations and emergency response systems. Ask your case manager.

**Can I use my HSA or FSA?**
Possibly. Some home safety costs may qualify with a letter of medical necessity. Check with your plan administrator.

**Are home safety costs tax deductible?**
Some home modifications made for medical reasons may count as medical expenses on your taxes. Check with your tax advisor.

**Is financial help available for home modifications?**
Some local agencies and nonprofits help with home modification costs. Your local Area Agency on Aging is a good place to start. We are happy to point you in the right direction during your consultation.

## Veterans

**I'm a veteran. Will the VA pay for this?**
No. This service is not paid by the VA. However, the Department of Veterans Affairs may pay for home safety items and home modifications that Medicare does not cover, such as grab bars, bathroom safety equipment, and accessibility changes, for veterans enrolled in VA health care when a VA clinician finds them medically needed. When a duplicate service is available from the VA, Dr. L'HommeDieu will encourage you to try the VA first. If recommended items could be covered by the VA, Dr. L'HommeDieu will refer you to the VA.

**I'm not enrolled in VA health care. What should I do?**
Enrolling in VA health care is a good first step. Once enrolled, ask your VA primary care team about a home safety evaluation.

**Do you offer anything for veterans at no cost?**
Yes. Veterans enrolled in VA health care can schedule a free phone call to understand what the VA may provide and how to ask for it. Call (813) 867-3372 or email info@homesafety.solutions.
[Visit our Veterans page](https://www.homesafety.solutions/for-veterans)

**Why would you send me to the VA instead of doing the work yourselves?**
Dr. L'HommeDieu served for many years as a VA Home Safety Coordinator. If the VA can pay for what you need, you should use that benefit first. We will help you understand how.

**Can you send my report to my VA care team?**
Yes, with your written permission. Sharing it can help your VA team decide what the VA can provide.

## Home Safety Visits

**What happens during a Home Safety Visit?**
Dr. L'HommeDieu walks through the home with you, watches how daily tasks are done (like getting in and out of the shower, on and off the toilet, and up and down steps), checks lighting, flooring, entrances, and stairs, and takes photos of each concern.

**How long does a visit take?**
60 to 120 minutes, depending on the home and the person's needs. Visits with deep dives may take longer.

**What do I receive?**
A written photo report with a prioritized list of hazards and clear recommendations for each one. You will receive it within 48 hours after your visit. With your written permission, we can also send a copy to your doctor, therapist, or case manager.

**Should family members be there?**
Yes, if possible. The person who lives in the home should be present, and anyone who helps with care is welcome, in person or by phone or video.

**Do you install anything?**
No. We assess and recommend. You choose who does the work. This keeps our advice independent.

**I need a ramp. How long does it need to be?**
The ADA Standards for Accessible Design call for a maximum slope of 1:12 for ramps, meaning every 1 inch of vertical rise needs at least 12 inches of ramp length. So a 24-inch rise (a typical set of steps) needs a ramp about 24 feet long, plus level landings at the top and bottom. Steeper ramps can be unsafe, especially for wheelchairs and walkers.
To picture the length for your own entry, this free tool lets you enter your rise and see the ramp length and slope: [ramp.engineer](https://ramp.engineer). Bring your numbers to your Home Safety Visit and we can plan placement, landings, and turns together.

**What is a Right Home Assessment?**
A visit to help you decide whether a home will work long term, whether it's your current home or one you are thinking of buying or renting. It is $250.

**Can you assess a home I am thinking of buying?**
Yes. That is the [Right Home Assessment](https://www.homesafety.solutions/right-home). It checks whether a house fits the person who will live there, now and in ten years, before you buy, rent or move. It is $250 and offered only in person, inside our Tampa Bay service area.

**What is a Build Verify Visit?**
After the work is done, we come back and check that it matches the specifications, such as grab bar height and placement. It is $150.

## Ready for Discharge

**What is Ready for Discharge?**
An assessment of the home timed around a hospital or rehab discharge, so the home is ready before or right after the person comes home.

**When should we book it?**
As soon as a discharge date is being discussed. The earlier we see the home, the more can be ready on the first night home.

**Can it be done while my family member is still in the hospital?**
Yes. We assess the home, not the hospital care. A family member can meet us at the home or walk us through it by video. With written permission, we can send the report to the discharge planner or case manager.

**Can it be done virtually?**
Yes. A family member walks us through the home by video. Virtual is $175; in-home is $250.

**What if discharge is only a few days away?**
Choose rush scheduling within 48 hours for an additional $50.

**What if the discharge date changes?**
Call or email us as soon as you know. A change caused by a hospital stay or medical emergency never carries a fee.

**What happens if the home gets a Red rating?**
Red means a gap that cannot close by arrival day. We call the family the same day, and the discharge planner with your authorization. The written report and the follow-up call go over every Red and Yellow item, so everyone knows what has to change before the person comes home.

## Assistive Technology

**What is an Assistive Technology Consultation?**
We match equipment and technology to the person, such as mobility aids, bathroom equipment, reachers, voice-controlled devices, and home controls, based on their abilities, goals, and home.

**What does ATP mean?**
Assistive Technology Professional, a certification from RESNA. It shows advanced training in matching assistive technology to people with disabilities and older adults.

**Do you sell equipment?**
No. We recommend what fits, and you can buy it anywhere. We accept no payments from equipment companies.

**How much does it cost?**
$75 as a deep dive added to a core assessment. Included with Membership.

## Remote Caregiving

**What is a Remote Caregiving Plan?**
A complete, room-by-room plan for the technology that lets family support a loved one from a distance: fall detection, safe entry, video check-ins, lighting, stove and thermostat safety, and storm backup. A qualified installer carries it out, and we train your family to use it.

**What does it cost?**
$150 as a deep dive added to a core assessment. Included with Membership. A yearly Plan Review is $150. A Contractor Consultation is not included.

**Does it include a full home hazard check?**
The deep dive focuses on technology. The full home hazard check comes from the core assessment it is added to.

**What do I receive?**
A written room-by-room plan, an Alert and Response Plan, a Storm and Outage Plan, a Home Monitoring Agreement, one family training session by video, and one follow-up call after installation.

**Do you monitor my parent?**
No. We design the system and train your family. Alerts go to the people and services you choose. We do not provide 24-hour monitoring or emergency response. In an emergency, call 911.

**What if my parent does not want to be monitored?**
We start with their goals and concerns. The plan includes only what the person agrees to, or what their legal representative approves if they cannot decide for themselves. Every plan includes a written Home Monitoring Agreement.

**Do you put cameras in the home?**
Only where the person agrees. We do not recommend cameras in bedrooms or bathrooms. Many fall detection options work without cameras.

**Do I have to buy certain brands?**
No. We write specifications, so you can buy anywhere. We may name examples that meet the specifications, and we are never paid by the companies that make them.

**Who installs the devices?**
Family can often set up plug-in devices with our guidance by video. Hardwired items go to qualified installers, such as licensed electricians, security and low-voltage installers, and HVAC contractors. Gas ranges go to licensed gas contractors. You choose and pay the installer directly.

**Will it work during a hurricane?**
Every plan includes a Storm and Outage Plan that shows what keeps working without power or internet and what the backup plan is.

**I live out of state. Can you still help?**
Yes. Book a core assessment by video with a Remote Caregiving deep dive. The home must be in Florida, New York or Ohio, and family members can join from anywhere.

**How is this different from an Assistive Technology Consultation?**
An Assistive Technology Consultation matches equipment and technology to the person. A Remote Caregiving Plan designs the whole system that lets family support that person from a distance, including alerts, home access, training, and outage planning. Many families book both on one visit.

**What happens when needs change?**
Book a Remote Caregiving Plan Review ($150) yearly or after a change in health.

## Storm Ready

**What is a Storm Ready Audit?**
A review of how prepared the person and the home are for hurricanes and power outages: medical equipment that needs power, cooling, medications, evacuation plans, backup power, and how family stays in touch.

**How much does it cost?**
$75 as a deep dive added to a core assessment. Included with Membership. In person only.

**When should I book it?**
Before hurricane season, which begins June 1. Members can add the Storm Ready deep dive to their yearly visit at no extra cost.

**How do you prepare a home for hurricane season when someone uses oxygen or a powered bed?**
With a [Storm Ready Audit](https://www.homesafety.solutions/storm-ready). Dr. L'HommeDieu goes through every device that needs power and how long each can run on battery, backup power options and which ones need a licensed electrician, medicine that needs cold storage, keeping cool without air conditioning, and evacuation. You receive a written household plan the whole family can follow. Hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30, and the best time to plan is April and May.

**What if a storm is coming on the day of my visit?**
We will reschedule at no charge. There is never a fee when a hurricane watch, warning, or evacuation order is in effect.

**Do you install hurricane shutters or storm protection?**
No. We focus on the person's safety and readiness, not building protection.

## Contractors and Installers

**Do you do the construction or installation?**
No. We assess and write the specifications. A licensed contractor or qualified installer of your choice does the work.

**Why don't you do the work yourselves?**
When the same company assesses and builds, there's a reason to recommend more work. Keeping them separate means our recommendations are based only on what the person needs.

**Do you get paid by contractors?**
No. No referral fees. No commissions. No payments from contractors, installers, suppliers, equipment companies, or device makers.

**Can you recommend a contractor?**
Yes. See our Contractor Network. You are always free to choose your own.
[Contractor Network](https://www.homesafety.solutions/contractors)

**What is a Contractor Consultation?**
For $150, we prepare a contractor-ready prescription with room-by-room specifications and have one call with your contractor to answer questions before they quote. It is not included in the Remote Caregiving Plan and can be added to it.

**What should I look for in a contractor?**
A Florida license for the work, proof of insurance, required permits, a written quote for each item, and willingness to follow written specifications.

## Membership

**What does Membership include?**
One in-home visit each year with your full written report, three 15-minute telehealth check-ins between visits, every deep dive, and priority scheduling. Membership is for homes inside our in-person service area.

**How much is Membership?**
$600 per year, or $55 per month with a 12-month commitment.

**Can I cancel?**
Yes. See "Can I cancel my Membership?" under Cancellations and Refunds, or read the full Membership terms in our Cancellation Policy.
[Membership cancellation details](https://www.homesafety.solutions/policies#membership-cancellation)

**Does my membership renew automatically?**
Yes. We send a reminder by email at least 30 days before your renewal date. You can cancel before renewal at no charge.

## Privacy and Your Information

**Is my information private?**
Yes. Health information in your reports is protected under HIPAA. See our [Privacy page](https://www.homesafety.solutions/privacy).

**Can I share my report with family or others?**
Yes. Sign an Authorization to Release Home Safety Report and we will send it to the people you name. You can revoke it at any time in writing.

**Can you send my report to my doctor?**
Yes, with your written permission. Sign an Authorization to Release Home Safety Report naming your doctor, and we will send the report directly. Sharing it helps your care team understand your home and your daily routines.

**What do contractors and installers see?**
Only the specifications for the work. Contractor and installer documents contain no diagnoses, medications, or health history.

**Do you sell my information?**
No.

## Scheduling and Service Area

**Where do you provide in-home visits?**
Only inside the area on our [service area map](https://www.homesafety.solutions/service-area), about a 60-minute drive from Apollo Beach. Everywhere else in Florida, New York, or Ohio, visits are by telehealth.

**Where are virtual visits available?**
For homes in Florida, New York or Ohio. Home Safety Visits and Ready for Discharge can be done by video, and the Remote Caregiving and Assistive Technology deep dives can be added to a video visit. Right Home Assessments and Storm Ready are in person only.

**How soon can I get a visit?**
Most visits are scheduled within 3 to 5 business days. Need it within 48 hours? Choose rush scheduling for an additional $50.

**How long will the visit take?**
60 to 120 minutes, depending on complexity. Visits with deep dives may take longer.

**How do I schedule?**
Book a $50 consultation online, call (813) 867-3372, or email info@homesafety.solutions.

## For Professionals and Facilities

**Do you work with hospitals, rehab facilities, and case managers?**
Yes. We provide home safety assessments for discharge planning at $150 per case, or $1,400 for a ten-case pack ($140 per case).
[Visit our facilities page](https://www.homesafety.solutions/for-facilities)

**Can I refer a patient or client?**
Yes. Call (813) 867-3372 or email info@homesafety.solutions. With the person's permission, we will send you a copy of the report.

**Do you need a physician order?**
No. Our services are home safety and technology consulting and do not require a physician order. With the person's written permission, we send reports to the physician and care team.

**How quickly can you see a patient being discharged?**
Most visits are scheduled within 3 to 5 business days. Rush scheduling within 48 hours is available.

## Terms We Use

**What is discharge readiness?**
Discharge readiness means whether the home, the equipment and the people helping are ready to support a patient safely from the first day home after a hospital or rehab stay. Our [Ready for Discharge](https://www.homesafety.solutions/ready-for-discharge) visit rates it Green, Yellow or Red.

**What does aging in place mean?**
Aging in place means living safely and independently in your own home as you get older, instead of moving because the home no longer works for you.

**What is a home modification?**
A home modification is a change to the house itself, such as grab bars, a ramp, a wider doorway or a walk-in shower, that makes it safer and easier to live in. We recommend and specify modifications. You choose who does the work.

**What is STEADI?**
STEADI stands for Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths and Injuries. It is the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's standard approach for clinicians to screen for fall risk. Our Home Safety Visit includes a fall risk screening using the STEADI approach.

**What is an ATP?**
An ATP is an Assistive Technology Professional, certified by RESNA after meeting education and experience requirements and passing a national exam. Dr. L'HommeDieu holds this credential. See Assistive Technology above for more.
